stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most cities that launched door-to-door vaccination drives in the 2010s saw only modest gains in childhood immunization rates. Riverton, a mid-sized port city, was a striking exception to that pattern. ______ its rate climbed from 71 percent to 94 percent in just two years, a jump larger than that recorded by any other participating city.
explanation: The sentence before the blank says Riverton was an exception to the pattern of modest gains. The sentence after it backs up that same claim with vivid evidence: a 23-point jump, bigger than any other city's. Because sentence two confirms and strengthens sentence one, 'Indeed' is the right transition.

A.why: You saw a contrast between Riverton's big jump and the modest gains elsewhere, and you let that surface contrast drive your choice. But the sentence right before the blank already says Riverton was an exception. The jump confirms that claim instead of turning against it.

C.why: You treated the rise in the rate as one example drawn from a larger group. The rise isn't a sample of several exceptions. It is the evidence for the one exception already named, so it confirms the point rather than illustrating it.

D.why: You read a cause-and-effect link that isn't there. Being an exception didn't cause Riverton's rate to climb. The climb is the reason Riverton counts as an exception.

subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: One clear relationship: exception claim proven by data showing larger gain than other cities.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Astronomers value the planned Halvorsen Array for two separate capabilities. First, its twelve dishes can be linked electronically to act as a single telescope with extraordinary resolution. ______ the array can observe in several radio frequencies at once, allowing researchers to follow fast-changing sources such as pulsars without switching instruments.
explanation: The first sentence says there are two capabilities, and the second sentence gives the first one. The sentence after the blank gives the second: a new item of the same kind. An addition word is needed, so 'In addition' is correct.

B.why: You assumed the first capability produces the second. Linking dishes for resolution doesn't cause the array to observe in several frequencies at once. The two are independent features.

C.why: You read the second capability as replacing the first. The passage says astronomers value both, so nothing is being swapped out.

D.why: You mixed up reinforcing a point with adding one. 'In other words' would mean sentence two restates the resolution feature, but it describes a completely different capability, the second of the two.

subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: Parallel structure: 'First' capability followed by second; distractors contradict or misstate the relationship.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Nutritionist Ama Owusu argues that the fiber in whole lentils sharply slows the rate at which sugars from a meal enter the bloodstream. Her 2021 feeding trial offers strong support for that view. ______ participants who ate a lentil side dish with white rice showed blood-glucose peaks nearly 30 percent lower than those of participants who ate the rice alone, and the effect lasted well into the afternoon.
explanation: The sentence before the blank says the trial strongly supports Owusu's view. The sentence after it gives the striking result that shows how strong that support is. Because sentence two confirms and intensifies sentence one, 'Indeed' is the most logical choice.

A.why: You took the comparison between the two groups of participants as a contrast between the sentences. The lower peaks agree with the claim that the trial supports Owusu, so a word that pushes back doesn't fit.

B.why: 'Similarly' needs a second, parallel case that resembles the first. The glucose result isn't a separate case like the trial. It is the trial's own finding, so it reinforces the point rather than comparing it to something else.

D.why: You read the result as replacing something in the sentence before. Nothing is rejected or swapped out. The result supports exactly what came before.

subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: Evidence structure: claim about fiber, trial supports it, blank introduces specific numerical evidence.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Cover crops such as rye and clover, planted between growing seasons, benefit farms in several distinct ways. Their dense roots hold soil in place during winter storms, greatly reducing erosion. ______ when the plants are cut down in spring, they decompose into organic matter that helps the soil retain water through the dry summer months.
explanation: The first sentence says cover crops help in several ways. The second gives one benefit, erosion control, and the sentence after the blank gives another, water retention. A second, parallel item calls for an addition word, so 'Moreover' is correct.

A.why: You read the water-retention benefit as an example of the sentence right before the blank. It isn't a case of erosion control. It is a separate benefit, another member of the 'several ways'.

B.why: You sensed a shift, from winter to spring and from roots to decomposition, and read it as a contrast. Both sentences describe benefits pointing the same direction, so nothing is being conceded or reversed.

C.why: You assumed the erosion control causes the water retention. The decaying plant matter helps the soil hold water whether or not the roots prevented erosion. The two benefits are parallel, not cause and effect.

subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: List of benefits: one effect stated, blank adds second distinct benefit; structure is transparent.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Folklorists who study the Appalachian 'Jack tales' note that the stories served more than one purpose for the families who told them. They entertained children during long winter evenings, when farm work slowed and households gathered by the fire. ______ the tales handed down practical lessons, since Jack's success usually depended on patience, thrift, and a sharp eye for a stranger's intentions.
explanation: The first sentence says the tales served more than one purpose. The second names entertainment, and the sentence after the blank names a different purpose, teaching practical lessons. A new item of the same kind calls for 'Additionally'.

A.why: 'Specifically' would mean sentence two restates entertainment in sharper terms. Teaching lessons isn't a more precise version of entertaining children. It is a separate purpose.

B.why: You treated entertainment and instruction as opposites. The passage presents both as purposes the tales served, so the second sentence adds to the first and doesn't qualify it.

D.why: You assumed the lessons follow from the entertainment. The passage doesn't say the tales taught lessons because they were entertaining. It lists the two purposes side by side.

subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: List of purposes: entertained children, blank adds practical lessons; parallel structure is obvious.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Cleaner wrasses are small reef fish that feed on parasites picked from the bodies of much larger fish, and marine biologists describe them as remarkably bold in this work. ______ they routinely swim into the open mouths and gill chambers of predators such as groupers, which could swallow them in an instant but almost never do.
explanation: The sentence before the blank calls cleaner wrasses remarkably bold. The sentence after it gives vivid proof: they swim into predators' mouths. Because sentence two confirms and dramatizes the same claim, 'Indeed' is correct.

A.why: The phrase 'could swallow them... but almost never do' contains a contrast, and you let it steer you. That contrast sits inside the second sentence. The sentence as a whole supports the claim that the wrasses are bold.

B.why: You read the second sentence as replacing something in the first. The wrasses still feed on parasites. Swimming into mouths is how that bold behavior shows up, not a substitute for it.

C.why: 'Likewise' needs a second creature or behavior that resembles the first. The second sentence describes the same wrasses and the same boldness, so it reinforces the point rather than drawing a comparison.

subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: Claim ('remarkably bold') followed by specific example; distractors contradict or misframe the relationship.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: The Japanese woodblock technique known as bokashi, in which the printer wipes ink unevenly across a dampened block before pressing the paper, was prized for more than one effect. It allowed artists to produce smooth gradations of color, such as a sky fading from deep indigo to pale yellow. ______ it could suggest atmosphere and distance, making far-off mountains appear to dissolve into mist.
explanation: The passage says bokashi was prized for more than one effect. The sentence before the blank gives the first, color gradation, and the sentence after it gives a second, a sense of atmosphere and distance. Adding a parallel item calls for 'Moreover'.

B.why: You confused adding a new point with restating the old one. 'In short' would introduce a summary of the color-gradation effect, but the sentence after the blank introduces a second effect.

C.why: You treated the two effects as opposites. Both are reasons the technique was prized, so they point the same direction.

D.why: 'Otherwise' means 'if not' or 'in other respects' and sets up an alternative. The second effect doesn't depend on the first failing. It adds to it.

subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: Two effects of bokashi listed; blank adds second effect to parallel structure.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Meteorologist Rafael Duarte has long argued that the coastal city of Porto Salgado lies in an unusually persistent fog zone. Records from the city's airport, though collected for flight safety rather than for climate research, bear him out. ______ fog reduced visibility there to less than one kilometer on 187 days last year, more than at any other airport along that coast.
explanation: The sentence before the blank says the airport records support Duarte. The sentence after it gives the striking figure, 187 foggy days, that shows how strongly they support him. Because sentence two confirms the same point with vivid detail, 'In fact' is correct.

A.why: You reacted to the 'though' clause about flight safety and expected a reversal. The main claim of that sentence is that the records bear Duarte out, and the fog figure agrees with it.

C.why: You read the fog statistic as replacing something mentioned before. Nothing is rejected. The statistic is the evidence the previous sentence promised.

D.why: You reversed the logic. The records supporting Duarte don't cause 187 foggy days. The foggy days are what make the records support him.

subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: Claim about fog zone, records support it, blank introduces confirming data; one clear logical step.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most fruits store their energy as sugar and contain very little fat; an apple or a peach is typically less than 1 percent fat by weight. Nutrition researchers describe the avocado as a striking outlier among fruits. ______ roughly 15 percent of its flesh is fat, most of it the same monounsaturated oleic acid found in olive oil, which is why dietary guidelines often group avocados with nuts and oils rather than with other produce.
explanation: The sentence before the blank says the avocado is a striking outlier among fruits. The sentence after the blank backs that claim up with vivid evidence: about 15 percent fat, compared with less than 1 percent for most fruits, which is enough that guidelines group it with oils. Sentence two confirms and strengthens the same point, so it takes a reinforcing word. 'Indeed' does exactly that.

A.why: You saw '15 percent fat' set against the '1 percent' of apples and peaches and read it as a contrast. That contrast is between the avocado and other fruits, and the passage has already stated it. The sentence after the blank doesn't push back on the claim that the avocado is an outlier. It proves the claim, so a contrast word like 'nevertheless' reverses the logic.

C.why: You treated the fat content as a result of the avocado being an outlier. It works the other way round: the avocado counts as an outlier because of its fat content. Sentence two is evidence for sentence one, not a consequence of it.

D.why: You noticed that the two sentences point the same way and picked a same-direction word. 'Similarly' introduces a second, comparable case, though, and the sentence after the blank is still about the avocado. There is no second item to compare. The sentence reinforces the same claim, which calls for 'indeed', not a word of likeness.

subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Archaeologist Tomás Reyes argues that the clay tokens found in a Bronze Age storehouse in northern Mesopotamia served two distinct purposes. Incised lines on each token recorded how many measures of barley a household owed the temple. ______ because the tokens were sealed inside hollow clay balls that a witness stamped before the clay dried, an intact ball also functioned as a tamper-proof receipt: no one could alter the count without visibly breaking the seal.
explanation: The first sentence names a category with a count: two distinct purposes. The next sentence gives the first purpose, recording barley debts. The sentence after the blank gives the second purpose, serving as a tamper-proof receipt, and the word 'also' marks it as a new item. The two purposes are parallel, separate items pointing the same way, so the blank needs an addition word. 'Moreover' adds that second point.

A.why: 'Specifically' would mean the sentence after the blank restates the record-keeping purpose more precisely. That sentence introduces a different purpose, a seal against tampering, so it isn't zooming in on the first one. You mistook a new item for a sharper version of the old one.

B.why: The word 'because' inside the sentence after the blank made it feel causal. That cause, the stamped clay seal, sits inside sentence two. The receipt function doesn't follow from the lines that recorded barley owed. Sentence two doesn't result from sentence one. It is the second of two parallel purposes.

D.why: 'Indeed' would reinforce the claim just made, that the tokens recorded barley debts. The sentence after the blank doesn't strengthen that claim. It adds the second of the 'two distinct purposes', and the word 'also' signals the addition. You confused 'indeed', which doubles down on the same point, with 'moreover', which adds a new one.

subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
